items.title: Sustainability without the pharmacist is untested
items.whyItMatters: Rounds stopped in the first home during leave, and elsewhere they stopped in two of five homes after the pharmacist left (c2).
items.opportunity: Train a named deputy in each home and measure rounds held when the pharmacist is absent.

items.title: No local measure of reach or carried-out recommendations
items.whyItMatters: The first home's impression that medicines fell was never measured against how many residents were reviewed.
items.opportunity: Measure reach and implementation of recommendations from round notes and administration records.

items.title: Short-stay and cognitively impaired residents may be missed
items.whyItMatters: Programmes reach short-stay residents least, and residents who cannot speak for themselves depend on families who may not attend.
items.opportunity: Report reach by length of stay and by whether a substitute decision-maker took part.

items.title: Restarted medicines are rarely reported
items.whyItMatters: A stopped medicine that is restarted within weeks signals harm or a poor decision (c3's review found restarts rarely reported).
items.opportunity: Count restarts within 30 days from administration records as a balancing measure.

items.title: Fidelity is documented, not observed
items.whyItMatters: A checklist completion index relies on round notes.
items.opportunity: Use the index and observe one round per home per quarter.

errorsFound: The need's impression that medicines 'seemed to fall' in the first home is unmeasured and should not be used as a planning value.
reevaluation: The gaps confirm an implementation study that measures adoption, reach, carried-out recommendations and sustainability, with falls and restarts as balancing measures.
summary: Five gaps; sustainability and missing local measures are high severity.
